newsitem.title: UK: Barclays down as profit-takers move in.
newsitem.headline: Barclays down as profit-takers move in.

text.p: Shares in banking group Barclays Plc fell sharply for a second day on Tuesday, amid a bout of profit-taking after the stock's surge to a record peak at the end of last week, analysts and dealers said.
Dealers said Barclays had been weighed down by declining hopes that the bank would spin off its investment banking unit BZW, and as a rise in U.S. interest rates loomed.
"They have had a good run and the banks are now out of vogue," said one head of equity trading. "The stocks that have had a significant upward move are being hit on the downside."
The stock was down 46p or 3.7 percent at 11.98-1/2 stg by 1419 GMT -- the biggest decliner in the FTSE 100 -- in volume of 2.8 million shares.
Tuesday's loss came on top of a 40-1/2p drop on Monday due in part to a downgrade by analysts at Dresdner Kleinwort Benson to "hold" from "buy."

Others in the recently-buoyant bank sector also declined, with Abbey National Plc down 22-1/2p at 937, Bank of Scotland Plc off 10-1/2p at 403, Lloyds TSB Plc 20-1/2p lower at 595, National Westminster Bank Plc down 12-1/2p at 785-1/2 and Royal Bank of Scotland Plc 16-1/2p weaker at 610-1/2.
